messages:
maria_cs: Quick idea — start a short 'signal snaps' cadence: 2–3 concise customer signals from onboarding + renewal checks each week for product to triage. Short, focused, actionable. Thoughts?
sam_product: Love that. Can we include severity + frequency + one customer quote? Helps triage quickly.
lee_engineering: Also useful to add environment/route/model impacted — eng needs repro-ish signal sometimes.
olivia_success: CS can pull 3 items each week from onboarding tickets + check-in notes. Will need a tiny template.
maria_cs: Yep — thinking fields: summary, priority (P0/P1/P2), signal_source, occurrences, sample_quote, suggested_fix, owner. Quick template below. Keep it one-line bullets so product can skim.
```
- summary: "search embeddings returning unrelated product matches"
- priority: P1
- source: onboarding ticket #345; customer ACME Retail
- occurrences: 6 in last 2 weeks
- sample_quote: "search returns unrelated SKUs — customers can't find products"
- suggested_fix: "evaluate embedding model + add per-route candidate re-ranking; short-term: tweak tokenization"
- owner: cs -> product (paul)
```
sam_product: Nice. Can we add an impact metric (e.g., support load increase or NPS delta) as a one-liner?
olivia_success: Yes — I can include ticket count + NPS change where available. Will deliver first snap next Wed.
lee_engineering: From eng side, can we reserve ~0.5 engineer-week per month for spikes from these snaps? We can batch related fixes.
maria_cs: Proposed cadence: weekly 3-item snapshot, monthly 30-min deep-dive with product+eng for clustered signals. If no objections, start next Wed. @sam_product @lee_engineering
sam_product: +1 :thumbsup:
prio-bot: Created recurring calendar "Signal Snaps — CS->Prod" on Wednesdays 10:00. Invites sent to maria_cs, sam_product, lee_engineering, olivia_success.
maria_cs: Thanks — i'll post the first packet in this thread next Wed with a tiny CSV + links to supporting tickets.
__notes: No title field per agents.md; thread is a single continuous string of messages.
